name: Real Estate
summary: Turn property interest into a qualified viewing.
problem: A buyer comparing a Doha apartment with a Lusail development needs different information from an investor comparing rental potential. Separate those journeys before choosing creative or keywords.
journey: Project or area discovery → listing review → budget and purpose → agent conversation → viewing → offer
visibility: Publish accurate availability, unit details, location context and clear agent contact. Keep sold or withdrawn stock from generating avoidable enquiries.
trust: Use approved property imagery, floor plans and factual project information. Explain whether you represent a developer, an agency or a specific listing.
automation: Record purchase/rental intent, budget band, preferred area and timing; assign the right agent and schedule a viewing. Send reminders only with permission.
content: Property walk-throughs, area explainers, purchase-process questions and clearly dated availability updates.

faq.question: Should every project have a landing page?
faq.answer: Only when there is useful, distinct information and a maintained offer. Repeated pages with a different area name create confusion and maintenance debt.

name: Construction
summary: Make technical capability easier for procurement teams to evaluate.
problem: A construction buyer may shortlist suppliers long before requesting a quote. A Qatar-facing website should explain project types, service boundaries and evidence that supports procurement decisions.
journey: Capability research → relevant project review → technical enquiry → scope discussion → tender/proposal → procurement decision
visibility: Build pages around actual capabilities and project sectors, with contact paths for technical and commercial enquiries.
trust: Use approved project roles, dates and scope. Separate main-contractor, subcontractor and consultant experience; do not imply certifications you cannot document.
automation: Route enquiries by discipline, contract size and project stage. Track document requests and assign proposal deadlines to named owners.
content: Project methodology, quality-control processes, documented case studies and explainers of common scope decisions.

faq.question: Can marketing replace supplier qualification?
faq.answer: No. Marketing can make evidence easier to evaluate. Procurement qualification and approvals must be supported by the business itself.

name: Architecture & Interiors
summary: Move from visual inspiration to a well-qualified design brief.
problem: A prospect may admire an interior photograph without understanding your scope, fees or project fit. In Qatar, explain the property type, delivery approach and consultation process before asking for a detailed brief.
journey: Inspiration → scope and budget → consultation → site visit → proposal
visibility: Organize work by project type and services, not only by image style. Make fit-out, design-only and supervision boundaries clear.
trust: Credit photographers, collaborators and your precise role. Obtain permission before publishing private residences or identifiable client details.
automation: Capture property type, location, approximate budget and timing, then schedule a consultation and prompt proposal follow-up.
content: Before-and-after work with consent, material choices, design decisions and clear explanations of project stages.

faq.question: Should we publish a fixed price per square metre?
faq.answer: Only if it accurately reflects a defined scope. Explain what is included and where materials, approvals or site conditions change the quote.

name: Dental Clinics
summary: Help patients choose a consultation and keep the booking journey clear.
problem: A person searching for a dental service needs trustworthy information and a practical booking path. Keep clinical claims reviewed by the clinic and separate marketing qualification from medical advice.
journey: Service search → clinic and clinician information → booking enquiry → staff confirmation → appointment → permitted follow-up
visibility: Create accurate service pages and an eligible business profile. Explain appointment steps, opening hours and contact choices.
trust: Use clinic-approved clinician credentials and consented content. Do not invent outcomes, treatment guarantees or patient testimonials.
automation: Route appointment requests to staff, send permitted reminders and record cancellation/rescheduling. Automation should not diagnose or recommend treatment.
content: Clinic-reviewed service explanations, visit preparation, facility information and answers about booking logistics.

faq.question: Can a WhatsApp agent answer clinical questions?
faq.answer: Use it for approved administrative information and handoff. Clinical questions should go to an appropriately qualified professional.

name: Healthcare
summary: Make service navigation and appointment access easier.
problem: A healthcare group can have many departments and locations with different booking rules. Give Qatar patients and referring organizations accurate routing information without turning marketing copy into medical guidance.
journey: Department discovery → provider information → eligibility/logistics → staff triage → confirmed booking
visibility: Map departments, real locations and referral pathways to distinct, maintained pages.
trust: Use reviewed credentials and service information. Set a publication owner for updates and protect patient information in media and forms.
automation: Route administrative requests by department and preferred contact method. Avoid collecting medical histories in a general marketing lead form.
content: Facility access, appointment preparation, referral administration and approved provider introductions.

faq.question: Can we collect patient details through the marketing form?
faq.answer: Collect only what is necessary for an administrative enquiry. Clinical records require a separately designed, reviewed and secured workflow.

name: Restaurants & Hospitality
summary: Connect discovery with a visit, booking or repeat order.
problem: A diner comparing places in Doha may need a current menu, location, opening hours and a clear booking option. A hotel event enquiry needs a different path with capacity, dates and requirements.
journey: Discovery → menu or venue review → directions/booking/order → visit → permitted retention follow-up
visibility: Keep genuine locations, hours and menu information consistent. Separate dining, delivery and event enquiries.
trust: Use actual food and venue photography, accurate offer conditions and genuine customer feedback.
automation: Route bookings by date and party size; confirm with staff. Build consent-based follow-up for repeat visits rather than messaging every past contact.
content: Menu highlights, venue tours, seasonal offers with exact dates, dining logistics and event-space walkthroughs.

faq.question: Should offers change during Ramadan or events?
faq.answer: Plan around your real trading hours, capacity and customer needs. Publish accurate dates and conditions rather than assuming every audience follows the same pattern.

name: Beauty & Aesthetics
summary: Match enquiries with the right service and booking process.
problem: A salon appointment and a medical aesthetics consultation have different information needs. Build service journeys that clarify who provides the service, how booking works and what information staff should confirm.
journey: Service discovery → evidence and suitability information → booking request → staff confirmation → appointment → follow-up
visibility: Separate salon services from clinician-led services. Keep service availability and real location details current.
trust: Use consented imagery and reviewed claims. Do not imply guaranteed results or publish before-and-after material without approval.
automation: Capture requested service and appointment preference, then hand off suitability questions. Reminders and rebooking prompts need permission.
content: Service introductions, staff profiles, venue experience and administrative booking FAQs.

faq.question: Can ads promise a specific treatment result?
faq.answer: Avoid unsupported promises. Have qualified clinic staff review any medical service claims and applicable advertising requirements before use.

name: E-commerce
problem: A campaign can produce orders that are expensive to deliver or frequently cancelled. A Qatar growth plan should connect product margin, delivery coverage and checkout experience before scaling media.
journey: Product discovery → comparison → cart → checkout → fulfillment → repeat purchase
visibility: Improve category structure, product detail and delivery/returns information so shoppers can decide before checkout.
trust: Use genuine product imagery and accurate stock/offer conditions. Explain who handles support and returns.
automation: Connect order status, customer support routing and permission-based retention; reconcile campaign reporting with completed orders.
content: Product demonstrations, comparisons using verified specifications, customer-use guidance and delivery explainers.

faq.question: Should we optimize for revenue alone?
faq.answer: No. Include product margin, refunds, payment costs and fulfillment when judging whether a campaign can scale.

name: Professional Services
summary: Turn specialist expertise into a credible commercial conversation.
problem: Consultancies and B2B firms often sell work that cannot be understood from a short service list. Explain the decision you help a Qatar client make, the evidence you use and what the engagement delivers.
journey: Problem research → expert/service evaluation → initial brief → discovery → scoped proposal → engagement
visibility: Map pages to specific buyer problems and procurement questions. Avoid broad claims such as being the best without supporting evidence.
trust: Publish approved case scope, qualifications and useful analysis. Clearly separate illustrative scenarios from delivered results.
automation: Qualify company type, decision context, timing and budget; route the brief to the right specialist and track proposal follow-up.
content: Practical buyer guides, methodology explainers, sector perspectives and permission-cleared case studies.

faq.question: How much expertise should we share free?
faq.answer: Publish enough to help a buyer understand the problem and judge your approach. Reserve tailored diagnosis and implementation for the agreed engagement.
